readout_other: object recognition task; ELISA for BDNF, NGF-beta and cytokines; oxidative stress assays
direction_notes: LIPUS prevented the object-recognition deficit and increased BDNF and NGF-beta in the hippocampus of the beta-amyloid ICV model; neuroprotective aim.
safety_notes: The authors conclude chronic LIPUS treatment is safe, but no specific safety assessment is described.

timing.protocol_description: Treatment began 24 h after the beta-amyloid infusion and was given at 48-h intervals for 5 weeks (35 d), transcranially with conductive gel under isoflurane; sonication time per session is not stated.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The animals were randomly divided into three groups: control n = 8/group; $\beta \mathrm { { A } } _ { 1 - 4 2 }$ (400 pmol) ${ \bf { n } } = 9 /$ group; and $\beta \mathrm { { A } } _ { 1 - 4 2 }$ (400 pmol) + LIPUS n = 6/group.

flags.reason: Intensity of 0.8 W/cm2 is given without type or domain; placed as ispta in unspecified_domain on the assumption of a physiotherapy-device spatial-average temporal-average specification, which the paper does not say.

Central frequency 3.3 MHz +/- 10 percent from a commercial physiotherapy-type device (Ibramed); the field is a transcranial exposure of the whole head with a 7.0 cm2 effective radiating area, so the target is recorded as brain.
Manufacturer inferred from the citation '(Ibramed 2012)' after the parameter list; no model is named.
N = 23 rats overall in groups of 8, 9 and 6; figure legends report n = 9, 6 and 8 inconsistently. Recorded the LIPUS group size of 6.
